title: Unlocking the Full Potential of Smart Contracts | Sergey Nazarov
description:
Chainlink Co-Founder Sergey Nazarov explains how Chainlink Runtime Environment accelerates the development of advanced smart contracts across multiple blockchains, real-world data sources, identity and compliance systems, and traditional enterprise infrastructure, all in a privacy-preserving manner.

Chainlink is the industry-standard oracle platform bringing the capital markets onchain and powering the majority of decentralized finance (DeFi). The Chainlink stack provides the essential data, interoperability, compliance, and privacy standards needed to power advanced blockchain use cases for institutional tokenized assets, lending, payments, stablecoins, and more. Since inventing decentralized oracle networks, Chainlink has enabled tens of trillions in transaction value and now secures the vast majority of DeFi. 

Many of the world’s largest financial services institutions have also adopted Chainlink’s standards and infrastructure, including Swift, Euroclear, Mastercard, Fidelity International, UBS, S&P Dow Jones Indices, FTSE Russell, WisdomTree, ANZ, and top protocols such as Aave, Lido, GMX and many others. Chainlink leverages a novel fee model where offchain and onchain revenue from enterprise adoption is converted to LINK tokens and stored in a strategic Chainlink Reserve. Learn more at chain.link.

✅ Subscribe and turn notifications on: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCnjkrlqaWEBSnKZQ71gdyFA?sub_confirmation=1

Learn more about Chainlink:

Website: https://chain.link
Docs: https://docs.chain.link
Twitter: https://twitter.com/chainlink

#Chainlink #crypto #blockchain

asr.full_text: The Chainlink runtime environment seeks to simplify the creation of advanced smart contracts the way the Ethereum virtual machine simplified the initial creation of smart contracts. The Ethereum virtual machine allowed smart contracts to be created on one chain, but not to have any relationship to other chains or any data or any identity or anything else outside of those chains. Now, that Ethereum virtual machine, Ethereum are amazing technologies that have propelled our industry to new heights, created an exciting new trend of tokenization, the traditional finance community enabled DeFi to happen. So it's very exciting what they've done. But there really needs to be an environment that not only allows you to write a smart contract on one chain, there needs to be an environment that includes all the data, all the connections to all the other chains, all the identity, all the compliance services and tools, as well as all the different capacity to do the computations around all of those things. It also needs to provide it I think, in a very privacy preserving way, so that if you need data to be computed, and you need the data to be private, if you need the computation, relying on the data to be private, if you need the identity details of those involved in the transaction to be private, you can do that computation somewhere, you can gain access to the data easily, you can allow that computation to affect things on many hundreds of different chains, and you can write a single piece of code that defines all of that complexity in one place. So that's what the Chainlink runtime environment does, it creates a new environment in which you can write a single piece of code that defines the relationship of a smart contract across chains in relation to data, in relation to identity, in relation to traditional systems, and to do it in a privacy-preserving way such that all of those computations, all of that data, all of that identity can remain private, but still be computed in a way where you receive cryptographic proofs back that they were computed correctly. And so it can be relied upon just like the cryptographic proofs of a chain. And these cryptographic proofs are put on chains. They're put in other systems. They're put wherever you need proof that the computation that happened to change the runtime environment was done correctly. Fundamentally, I think what this will do is it will accelerate the development of more advanced smart contracts, like Next Generation DeFi, institutional smart contracts from traditional finance institutions. I think it will simplify the developer journey for Web 2 developers and Web 3 developers to use more chains and to do more transactions on existing chains so I think it's going to increase the transaction volume and usage of existing chains because it'll simplify the use of data on those chains. It'll simplify the connectivity between those chains. It'll simplify identity on those chains. It'll simplify all these key components that both are needed on a single chain for that single chain to be used correctly for these more advanced smart contracts and for usage across chains which is really the world we're now where there are silos of capital silos of contracts silos of data on different chains those silos need to be broken down and managed efficiently and you need a single place with a single piece of code that says, this is my application's relationship with these 50 chains. This is my application's relationship to this piece of data in relation to the contractual conditions on those chains. This is my application's relationship with all the identity requirements that I need to fulfil in being able to transact on those chains in a regulated compliant way this is the complexity that i think only the chain link runtime environment solves right now there really is no other system with this collection of different um services data services cross-chain services identity services compliance services all in a single place so all of those services don't even exist in a single place much less there being a way to compose all those services with a single piece of code across hundreds of chains. So it's something that I think is pretty unique. I'm very excited by the adoption we're seeing both in the Web3 community, the DeFi community and the TradFi community. And I think the Chainlink runtime environment is really going to be able to take both the Chainlink ecosystem and the entire industry to the next level so I'm really looking forward to what is going to happen there and it's constantly being improved there's new services new capabilities there's also a direction where there are third parties building new services and capabilities to be available as workflows or components of workflows. There's a community of people building things into the CRE as we speak, and that's also very exciting. So I'm really looking forward to next stages of the CRE and what it's going to do both for our industry and for the Chainlink ecosystem.
